answer: Assay-table bond: each identity locks 80 credits, registers one crystal, and files an assay table listing the pigment dose per layer. Auditors recompute every pigment level from the published quartz table and burn the bond on a reused quartz table or a mismatched dose, so a rented-crystal ring fails. The k-th assay costs 42+9(k-1); 1,000 fakes cost 4,537,500 plus 80,000 locked against a 40,000 pool. Honest identities pay 42 once, keep the bond.
